data.long_meaning: The name Regulan is derived from the Latin word 'regulus', which means 'ruler' or 'governor'. In Christian tradition, this name was often given to children born into positions of authority or power. The name Regulan carries the meaning “Ruler, Governor” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English. Parents who choose Regulan usually hope their child will grow to embody ruler, governor and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes leadership, governance, and the responsibility of ruling with wisdom and justice.

in_hebrew.name: רגולן
in_hebrew.long_meaning: רגולן הוא שם עברי שמשמעותו 'בן הרגל', כלומר, 'בן ההליכה' או 'בן הדרך'. השם נראה לראשונה בקשר לאדם חסיד, שהצטיין במסירותו ובאדיקותו. השם יכול להיות קשור לבן הדור הבא, או לאדם שמסיר עצמו למען הנהגת הדרך.

in_greek.name: Ρεγούλας
in_greek.long_meaning: Ὁ ὄνομα Ρεγούλας (Ρεγούλας) ὑποδηλώνει τὴν ὑποστάσιν τοῦ υἱοῦ τῆς ὁδοῦ, ἡ ὁποία εἶναι ἡ ὁδος τοῦ Θεοῦ. Ἡ ὁδος τοῦ Θεοῦ εἶναι ἡ ὁδος τῆς ἀλήθειας, ἡ ὁδος τῆς ἐμπειρίας, ἡ ὁδος τῆς σωτηρίας. Ὁ Ρεγούλας εἶναι ὁ ὁποῖος ἀκολουθεῖ τὴν ὁδόν, ὁ ὁποῖος περιπατεῖ σὲ τὴν ὁδόν, ὁ ὁποῖος ζων ἐπὶ τὴν ὁδόν.

in_latin.name: Regulanus
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Regulanus derivatur a verbo Greco via, quod significat iter, via, itinere. Filius viae, id est, Filius iteris, significat filium qui viae Domini secutus est. Via Domini est via veritatis, via experientiae, via salutis. Regulanus est qui via Domini secutus est, qui iterum in via Domini ambulat, qui in via Domini vivit.

historical_references.reference: Regulan was the name of a sect of heretics in North Africa during the 4th and 5th centuries, who rejected the authority of the Roman bishops and followed a more ascetic and communal lifestyle. They were named after the Carthaginian bishop Regulus, who was renowned for his austere and disciplined life.

The term 'Regulan' was also used to describe a sect of Italian monks in the 11th century, who lived in communal monasteries and were known for their strict observance of the monastic rules. They were inspired by the writings of the Benedictine monk Peter Damian, who advocated for a return to the original spirit of monasticism.
